blocks.text: After configuring the integration between Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and Zscaler Deception and deploying the necessary decoys, you can use the decoys to set up lures for attackers. You can use different methods to set up lures depending on the type of decoys, as explained in the following sections:

blocks.item: Service Account Decoys

A service account in GCP is a special type of account used by applications or services to authenticate and interact with Google Cloud resources. A service account is identified by its unique email address. You can create service account decoys with API credentials that can be placed on endpoints using the following landmine decoys:
Cloud Lures
File Decoys via Credential Files
If an adversary enumerates these, the event is logged as an attack. You can view and analyze the attack details from the Deception dashboard.
To learn more about service accounts in GCP, refer to the Google documentation.
Cloud Storage Decoys

Google Cloud Storage is an object-based storage service on GCP. You can create cloud storage decoys and associate file datasets. Optionally, the URLs of cloud storage decoys can be added to a landmine policy to add lures to the endpoints. The cloud storage decoys can detect the following attack paths:
Public: Adversaries can enumerate public cloud storage by using keywords related to an organization to find exposed cloud storage accounts on the internet in an attempt to steal sensitive data.
Private: Adversaries with compromised identities of your organization can target cloud storage accounts that are accessible via the compromised identities.
An interaction with the cloud storage decoy is logged as an attack. You can view and analyze the attack details from the Deception dashboard.
To learn more about cloud storage in GCP, refer to the Google documentation.
Cloud SQL Decoys

The cloud SQL in GCP is a service that allows you to set up and host relational databases (MySQL or PostgreSQL). You can create cloud SQL decoy databases (public or private) based on MySQL or PostgreSQL to lure adversaries that are looking for databases to disrupt services or steal data. Optionally, the credentials of the master user (or root) of the database along with the URL can be added to a landmine policy as a lure.
Any interaction with the cloud storage decoy is logged as an attack. You can view and analyze the attack details from the Deception dashboard.
To learn more about cloud SQL in GCP, refer to the Google documentation.
Secret Manager Decoys

A secret manager in GCP is a service used to securely store, manage, and control access to sensitive information such as API keys, passwords, certificates, and tokens. Secrets are stored centrally and accessed by applications through authenticated requests based on IAM permissions. You can create secret manager decoys containing fake secret identifiers or access references.
Any interaction with the cloud storage decoy is logged as an attack. You can view and analyze the attack details from the Deception dashboard.
To learn more about secret manager in GCP, refer to the Google documentation.
Artifact Registry Decoys

An artifact registry in GCP is a service used to store and manage software artifacts such as container images and language packages. Artifact registry repositories provide secure storage for build outputs used in application deployment. You can create an artifact registry with decoy artifacts.
Any interaction with the cloud storage decoy is logged as an attack. You can view and analyze the attack details from the Deception dashboard.
To learn more about artifact registry in GCP, refer to the Google documentation.
